subject: Pilot criteria & action items — inference economics focus
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@helixdata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-01T14:20:00Z
Subject: Follow-up & summary — inference economics discussion (today)

Tom — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Key pain points you shared:
- Token and per-request spend spikes during peak clinical ingestion windows (weekdays 09:00–12:00 PT).
- Unpredictable tail latency at the 95/99p during batch exports causing backlog in downstream pipelines.
- Desire to reduce per-active-user inference cost ~30–50% while preserving generation quality for clinical summarization.

Current stack you described:
- Primary: Managed API (vendor) for generation; separate self-hosted GPUs used for embeddings and small routing models.
- Traffic: median request length ~120 tokens; occasional long UIs up to 1,200 tokens; 10x delta between median and peak QPS.

Success criteria (what would make a pilot successful):
- 35%+ unit cost reduction vs current managed API over representative workload.
- 95th pctile latency <= 300ms for 90% of interactive calls.
- No degradation in ROUGE-style evals on your clinical summarization prompt set.

What Redwood proposes for initial pilot:
1) 2-week scoped pilot running a representative traffic replay (you provide sample logs/prompts).
2) Baselines: current managed API cost + Redwood Dedicated with batching, prefix caching, and optional int8 quantized variant.
3) Observable success metrics: cost per token, per-inference latency distribution, quality delta on your eval set.
4) Security: we can start with a short SOC2 questionnaire and put the pilot behind a VPC connector if needed.

Next steps / asks from your side:
- Share ~48–72 hours of anonymized request logs + representative prompt set (CSV attached as example).
- Confirm openness to evaluating a quantized model (we'll run quality checks first).
- Point to an internal owner for procurement/PO questions for a pilot credit agreement.

Attachments: redwood-econ-one-pager.pdf, example-prompt-set.csv

I'll draft a short mutual action plan once I get the logs. Monica (cc) will help with the replay and metric dashboards. Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@helixdata.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>, Sarah Collins <sarah@nimblehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & summary — inference economics discussion (today)

Rishi — thanks for the clear notes. All looks accurate. A few clarifications / answers below:

- Logs & prompts: I'm attaching a sanitized 72h sample (will share via Drive link to security team afterwards).
- Quantization: our ML team is open to int8/int4 if we can validate no meaningful quality regression.
- Procurement: we can do a pilot credit/MoU; procurement will want a short SOW and a one-page MSA appendix for pilots. Our finance contact is Sarah Collins (cc).

Quick numbers you asked for:
- Current managed API spend (monthly, prod): ~$42k.
- Average tokens per request (prod): 114 median, 980 95p.
- Peak QPS during ingestion windows: ~85 sustained for ~20 minutes; bursts to ~240 for <2m.

Questions:
1) How much setup time do you expect for a replay pilot (our infra team has limited cycles this month)?
2) Do you require raw payloads or are hashed request/response pairs sufficient for initial economics runs?

Thanks — Tom

Tom Reynolds
Head of Data Platforms | HelixData
tom@helixdata.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@helixdata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-02T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & summary — inference economics discussion (today)

Tom — great, appreciate the numbers. Short answers to your questions and a proposed mutual action plan below.

Setup estimate:
- We can run an initial dry-run within 48 hours of receiving hashed payloads and the prompt CSV. Full fidelity replay with payloads will take ~3 business days to validate.
- If you only can provide hashed request/response pairs, that's fine for cost/latency modeling; for quality checks we will need the actual outputs or a way to run the model on the prompts.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) By 2027-05-04: HelixData provides 72h hashed logs + prompt CSV + HubSpot SOW contact (Drive link or HubSpot record OK).
2) 2027-05-05 — 2027-05-12: Redwood runs replay on Dedicated infra + small quantized variant, produces cost delta and latency distribution report.
3) 2027-05-13: Review call (30m) to go over metrics, quality delta, and next steps for an extended pilot or production rollout.

Pilot governance and credits:
- Redwood can provide a pilot credit up to $10k for the initial two-week replay and setup. Any sustained Dedicated capacity beyond the pilot would require a short reserved capacity commitment (we can make the ask minimal for the first 90 days).

Please confirm if the timeline works and we'll send a short two-page SOW + pilot appendix for signatures. Monica will own the replay run — cc'd.

Thanks — Rishi
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@helixdata.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & summary — inference economics discussion (today)

Tom — thanks, I have visibility into scheduling the replay. Two quick operational notes:

- Please upload the sample logs and prompt CSV to the shared Drive folder (link above) and add read permissions for monica@redwood.inference.
- For hashed payloads, include a random id for each request so we can correlate replayed calls back to your latency buckets.

I'll kick off the dry-run as soon as files are in place and update the HubSpot deal with the MA-Plan milestones.

Monica
Senior Customer Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.inference
